title: Cyclotomic induction bimodules are projective and the comparison exact sequence
strategy:
Write $S=R( eta+i)$, $A=R^\Lambda( eta)$, $e_R=e( eta,i)$ and $e_L=e(i, eta)$. PBW gives finite right $A[t]$-projectives $K_0=Se_R/Sa(x_1)R( eta)e_R$ and $K_1=Se_L/Sa(x_2)R_1( eta)e_L$. With source $\kappa=-	au_{native}$, define $P(u)=u a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ and $Q(v)=v g_n\cdots g_1$, where unequal $g=\kappa$ and equal $g=(y-x)-(y-x)^2\kappa$. Moving each dot/crossing gives block bilinearity; expanding the cyclotomic ideal by the left cosets shows $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0	o R^\Lambda( eta+i)e_R)$. The local quadratic/braid calculation gives $QP=a_i(t)\prod_{
u_a

u_a}(t,x_a)$, with a uniform unit leading coefficient; consequently $P$ is injective. This is an actual monic comparison, not a filtered-colon citation.
The target is killed by a central monic dot polynomial. For a projective $A[t]$-resolution $0	o P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0	o M	o0$ and central monic $fM=0$, factor $f=jh$; injectivity gives $hj=f$. Each $P_r/fP_r$ is projective over $A$ by monic division, so the sequence for multiplication by $f$ splits over $A$. A splitting $pf=1$ yields $phj=1$, making $M$ projective. In the graded standard case keep the degree-zero part of the splitting. Apply this to $K_1,K_0$ and the target. The generator-fixing anti-involution gives the left counterpart; restriction of target projectives and induction now preserve projectives. Tensor exactness of the comparison follows because the target is right $A$-projective, and its functor sequence has target category $R( eta+i)$-modules. The same P/Q and monic splitting argument is valid ungraded for arbitrary monic deformation coefficients; degrees concern only the homogeneous branch.

axiom_use: None: the explicit P/Q polynomial comparison, monic projective-dimension-one resolution and finite splitting argument use only finite bimodule computations; no generic faithfulness, factorial inversion or choice is assumed.
